item.title: AI for Corporations: How to Scale Solutions Without Breaking the Bank on IT Infrastructure
item.description:
Hello, Habr! In a couple of weeks, on November 30th, we will hold a free webinar "AI for Corporations: How to Scale Solutions and Not Go Broke on IT Infrastructure." item.title: AI Assistant for an Automation Engineer
item.description:
Automation engineering is becoming a bottleneck: innovation cycles are shrinking, system complexity is growing, and experienced engineers are scarce. Major vendors are responding with AI assistants, but typically within their own ecosystems. In this article, I, Tatyana Pchelnikova, a product owner in Severstal's IT team for developing open automation system components, will explain how we decided to create an intelligent assistant and integrate it into our SeverCode (Flogic) development environment – and why openness is fundamental here. Read more

item.title: Google is trying to move site links to the very bottom of AI Overviews: why being named in the answer is more important for a site
item.description:
If a site gets traffic from Google, its link in AI Overviews might move to the very bottom of the answer: Google is currently testing this format. AI Overviews, or Google AI summaries, are a block with a neural network's answer above the regular search results. Previously, source site icons were at the top of this block. There is no click data for the new format yet, but even with the old format, clicks on sources within the overview were very rare. It is now more important for a site to be mentioned in the answer text itself, where a brand or fact is stated, than to simply appear in the list below it. Read more

item.title: OpenAI doubles free ChatGPT subscriptions for scientists to 200,000, but now offers ChatGPT Plus
item.description:
In July, OpenAI launched the 'ChatGPT for Academic Researchers' program, offering free ChatGPT access to 100,000 scientists, mathematicians, and engineers from selected higher education institutions worldwide. The company is now doubling the initiative's participants to 200,000, but they will receive access to ChatGPT Plus instead of ChatGPT Pro. Read more

item.title: Weights for the LongCat-2.5 model with 1.6 trillion parameters, deployed without NVIDIA, have been released
item.description:
Chinese delivery platform Meituan has released the weights for its multimodal MoE model LongCat-2.5, boasting approximately 1.6 trillion parameters with about 48 billion active per token, under a permissive MIT license. Notably, the model was trained without Western accelerators, and its official deployment guide contains no instructions for NVIDIA GPUs. The weights are now available on the Hugging Face repository. Read more

item.title: How to Read Texts in the Age of Slop
item.description:
Generative AI has made content creation easier, but modern hardware can produce cheap tokens at high speeds, even from large language models. This presents a significant problem. A year ago, Graham Neubi, a researcher at Carnegie Mellon University, offered a symbolic $50 reward to anyone who could use an AI detector to check scientific papers and reviews submitted to the International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR). The call came in November 2025, during the review process for ICLR 2026 papers, due to numerous complaints from researchers about vague, uninformative feedback, requests for unusual research, and citations to non-existent works. This led to suspicions that reviewers were outsourcing their work to machines. It's hard to blame them, as ICLR reviewers are machine learning researchers who typically aren't paid for their work. Read more

item.title: How to Secure Data in AI Systems if You're a D&D Dwarf
item.description:
Hello, Habr! AI systems are being implemented everywhere, leading to specific threats targeting AI infrastructure and the information security of systems that use it. Ensuring data confidentiality, integrity, and availability is paramount for both developers and users. This article touches upon some methods for secure data handling in AI training, but it's not a comprehensive guide to AI implementation. Its main goal is to introduce basic data privacy techniques using simple language and a humorous D&D analogy for enthusiasts. Read more

item.title: What to Assign to AI in the Finance Department: Four Areas of Application
item.description:
While companies are still deciding what constitutes AI transformation and where to place AI agents, the finance department continues with its usual schedule – needing to finalize the new budget and explain why the old one went over budget. My team automates data collection and the preparation of regulatory and management reporting, including plan-vs-actual. Our users and clients are most often finance specialists. I know their pain points and tasks best. I've identified four areas where AI can already help with routine tasks and free up time for what matters most – analyzing business results. At the end, I'll provide a cheat sheet with almost a hundred application ideas. This article is based on my presentation at the VBA forum and a webinar on management accounting. Read more

item.title: ChatGPT Recommends Us. I'm Checking Which Queries Lead to This
item.description:
Clients of one of the projects have started mentioning more often that GPT recommended us. I checked the suggested queries on another account and got our website listed first. I'll explain how to check recommendations for your niche, where to get search query statistics, and what prevents the neural network from reading a website. I'll also cover JavaScript, search bots, and the limitations of such checks.

item.title: AI tests are green, but the refund doesn't work: analyzing and fixing a draft API autotest
item.description:
I've been writing API autotests for a long time, and in recent months, I've been reviewing tests written not by humans, but by an IDE agent. They write quickly and accurately. The problem is different: such a test often verifies not a requirement, but how the API responds right now. It's stable, green, and cements a bug instead of catching it. In the article, I'll analyze a typical draft test for order refunds: what's wrong with it, how to spot it during a review, and what a trustworthy test looks like. The code is in pytest, but the ideas are language-agnostic. Read on
